title: Abhidhamma Piṭaka

attribution.tradition: The tradition's account (Atthasālinī, Nidānakathā): the Buddha taught the Abhidhamma in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven during the rains retreat after the Twin Miracle, to the gods led by his mother; each day he gave the method (naya) to Sāriputta at Lake Anotatta, who taught it to his five hundred pupils; it was recited at the First Council.

tradition.text: taught by the Buddha (5th c. BCE on the traditional chronology)

structure.description: seven books: Dhammasaṅgaṇī, Vibhaṅga, Dhātukathā, Puggalapaññatti, Kathāvatthu, Yamaka, Paṭṭhāna

summary: The third basket of the Pali canon: seven treatises that analyse experience into ultimate constituents (dhammas), classify them by matrices of triads and dyads, and set out their conditional relations; for the Theravāda the Buddha's teaching 'in terms of ultimate reality'.

title: Cūḷavaṃsa
summary: The continuation of the Mahāvaṃsa; chapter 37 tells the story of Buddhaghosa's coming to Lanka and the writing of the Visuddhimagga.

title: Buddhaghosuppatti
summary: A late legendary biography of Buddhaghosa.

title: Gandhavaṃsa
summary: A Burmese Pali catalogue of Pali authors and books.

title: Sāsanavaṃsa
summary: Paññāsāmi's Burmese Pali history of the dispensation in the Theravāda lands, completed in 1861.

title: Vipassanā Dīpanī (Manual of Insight, Ledi Sayadaw)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw's manual of insight: the perversions of perception, the three characteristics, the three kinds of full understanding, and how insight is developed.

title: Bodhipakkhiya Dīpanī (Manual of the Requisites of Enlightenment)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw's exposition of the thirty-seven requisites of awakening, urging their development in the present age of the dispensation.

title: Ānāpāna Dīpanī (Manual of Respiration)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw's manual of mindfulness of breathing as the basis for insight.

title: Maggaṅga Dīpanī (Manual of the Path Factors)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw on the eight path factors.

title: Niyāma Dīpanī (Manual of Cosmic Order)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw's treatise on the five orders (niyāma) of nature: seasons, seeds, kamma, mind and Dhamma.

title: Uttamapurisa Dīpanī (Manual of the Excellent Man)
summary: Ledi Sayadaw on the qualities of the superior person who strives for liberation.

title: Manual of Insight (Vipassanā Shunikyan)
summary: Mahāsi Sayadaw's large Burmese treatise on the theory and practice of insight meditation, written in 1944–45.

title: Practical Insight Meditation: Basic and Progressive Stages
summary: Mahāsi Sayadaw's instructions: noting the rising and falling of the abdomen, walking meditation, noting in daily activity, and the stages the meditator passes through.

title: The Progress of Insight (Visuddhiñāṇakathā)
summary: Mahāsi Sayadaw's Pali treatise describing, from practice, each insight knowledge from the discernment of mind and matter to reviewing knowledge.

title: The Heart of Buddhist Meditation
summary: Nyanaponika Thera's presentation of satipaṭṭhāna as 'bare attention' according to the Mahāsi method, with an anthology of texts.

title: The Essentials of Buddha-Dhamma in Meditative Practice
summary: Sayagyi U Ba Khin's short exposition of sīla, samādhi and paññā, and of the awareness of anicca through the body as the way to nibbāna.

title: The Discourse Summaries (S. N. Goenka)
summary: Condensed evening talks of the ten-day Vipassana course, day by day.
notes: Condensed by William Hart; the talks themselves are oral.

title: The Art of Living: Vipassana Meditation as Taught by S. N. Goenka
summary: William Hart's account of Goenka's teaching and the ten-day course.

title: Knowing and Seeing
summary: Talks and questions by Pa-Auk Sayadaw setting out the Pa-Auk sequence: mindfulness of breathing and jhāna, four-elements meditation, discernment of materiality and mentality, dependent origination and insight.

title: The Workings of Kamma
summary: Pa-Auk Sayadaw's exposition of kamma according to the Abhidhamma, with the discernment of past causes.

title: Muttodaya (A Heart Released)
summary: Teachings of Ajahn Mun recorded by his disciples: the heart's radiance, defilements as visitors, and the practice of body contemplation.

title: Venerable Ācariya Mun Bhūridatta Thera: A Spiritual Biography
summary: Ajahn Maha Boowa's biography of Ajahn Mun (Thai 1971): his dhutaṅga life, meditative experiences, visions, teaching and attainment, as the tradition tells them.

title: Arahattamagga, Arahattaphala: The Path to Arahantship
summary: A compilation of Ajahn Maha Boowa's talks on the last stages of practice, including the danger of attachment to the radiant citta.

title: Keeping the Breath in Mind (Method 2)
summary: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo's instructions in breath meditation: adjusting the breath, the bases of the breath in the body and spreading breath energy, and developing discernment from concentration.

title: Food for the Heart
summary: Collected talks of Ajahn Chah: virtue, concentration and wisdom as one path, letting go, uncertainty (mai nae) and the middle way.

title: A Still Forest Pool
summary: Short teachings of Ajahn Chah compiled by Jack Kornfield and Paul Breiter.

title: Handbook for Mankind (Khu Mue Manut)
summary: Buddhadāsa's lectures on the essentials: suffering, the three characteristics, 'I' and 'mine', the three trainings and nibbāna here and now.

title: Ānāpānasati: Mindfulness with Breathing
summary: Buddhadāsa's full manual of the sixteen steps of mindfulness with breathing.

title: Heartwood of the Bodhi Tree
summary: Buddhadāsa's talks on voidness (suññatā) as the heart of the Buddha's teaching and on working with a void mind.

title: Paṭiccasamuppāda: Practical Dependent Origination
summary: Buddhadāsa's presentation of dependent origination as arising in everyday experience from sense-contact, criticizing the exclusively three-lives reading.

title: Buddhadhamma
summary: P. A. Payutto's systematic exposition of the Buddha's teaching from the Pali canon and commentaries.

title: The Dhammakaya Case (Korani Thammakai)
summary: P. A. Payutto's critique of the Dhammakāya movement's teaching that nibbāna is a self (attā), arguing from the canon and commentaries that nibbāna is not-self.

title: The Yogāvacara's Manual
alt_titles: The Yogāvachara's Manual of Indian Mysticism as Practised by Buddhists

attribution.tradition: a yogāvacara's handbook of the old kammaṭṭhāna
attribution.scholarly: a manuscript from 18th-c. Sri Lanka connected with the Siamese ordination lineage; edited by T. W. Rhys Davids (PTS 1896), translated by F. L. Woodward as Manual of a Mystic (PTS 1916)

summary: A Sinhala-Pali manuscript manual of the old (borān) meditation: preliminary rites, the five kinds of rapture, the tranquillities and other qualities to be induced in order at points of the body, and the path attainments.
notes: Content summarized from memory at a general level only (low confidence on details).
